description.narrative: SC and Bayader will work together in SC’s Primary Health Care Clinics (PHCC) in Deir Al Balah and Khan Younis to improve access to integrated primary health care, and increase hygiene awareness and access to reduce waterborne and infectious diseases. The project will target 24000 people.SC will lead on health: 1) provision of integrated support for patients experiencing gender-based violence (GBV), mental distress, and children facing abuse or exploitation; 2) General outpatient consultations and comprehensive sexual and reproductive health (SRH) services, incl. antenatal & postnatal care and family planning; 3) health education and awareness sessions to promote healthy behaviors.Bayader will lead on WASH: 1) hygiene & sanitation promotion sessions in the PHCCs to raise awareness on infectious diseases and how to mitigate them; 2) provision of hygiene items to enhance beneficiaries' access to sanitation products.

Save the Children (SC) and Bayader for Environment and Development Association (Bayader) will provide primary health care and promote good hygiene practices to reduce hygiene-related health issues.The ongoing war in Gaza has a devastating impact on health systems and the health of the besieged population, affecting physical and mental well-being. The health system is at the brink of collapse; only 14 out of 36 hospitals are partially functioning, while primary health centres and medical points have suspended operations. Women, children and newborns are particularly affected, as access to essential maternal, newborn, and child health services remains extremely limited, e.g. up to 5 newborns share a single incubator (SC, Sept. 2025).The war has also decimated Gaza’s WASH infrastructure, leaving communities at severe risk of waterborne diseases and other public health emergencies. 95% of the population is facing water insecurity. Diarrhoeal diseases among children under five have surged by over 2,000%, with 71,000 cases reported in a single week, and 39% of all non-trauma morbidity due to diarrhoeal disease (SC, Sept. 2025). Women and girls face heightened challenges, incl. pregnancy-related risks, urinary tract infections, and protection concerns when attempting to access scarce WASH resources. 87% of surveyed people reported deteriorating sanitation conditions due to scarcity and lack of availability of sanitation goods, which is causing the spread of preventable infectious diseases (WASH LTM, June 2025).

While the health activities will be available for all PHCC visitors, we expect & aim to reach mainly women, as primary caregivers, and girls (>60%). The WASH component will target specific patients attending the PHCCs. Beneficiary selection will rely on clinic attendance records & vulnerability screening, prioritizing women, displaced families, people with disabilities, elderly, women-headed & low-income HHs, and caregivers with children <5. A gender & age-sensitive approach will be applied. Special consideration will be given to survivors of violence & persons with chronic diseases whose hygiene risks are higher. SC implements its Disability Inclusion Policy, ensuring accessibility for children & adults with disabilities (e.g. PHCCs are wheelchair accessible). The design is based on need assessments and aligned with UN OCHA third reserve allocation priorities, ensuring the activities respond to the priority needs of people in an adequate manner.
